claim: The requirement that the entries of `tasks/RENUMBERED.md` live in per-session files «як журнали задачі 739, щоб сам файл не конфліктував» may no longer be needed: after the owner's amendment only the runner runs `renumber`, so the map has one writer and could be a plain file the runner appends to and commits; the old-name lookup for inbox answers stays the same. The words «поруч із `journal.py fold` (задача 739)» on line 41 lean on the same assumption and point at a runner step that does not exist.

evidence.detail: The design gave `renumber` two callers: the runner after `sync_branch` and a cloud session after merge. The session-file rule on lines 81-83 is there so those two writers do not conflict on the map.
Owner's answer (4): «так, але однакові номери розводить лише runner після синхронізації гілки — хмарних сесій зараз немає». The second writer is removed.
The task itself says «Запускає лише runner», yet lines 45-46 keep the per-session-file rule written for two writers.
`sync_branch` is called here; a grep for `journal.py` in board-runner.sh finds nothing, so the runner has no `journal.py fold` step for `renumber` to stand beside.
Per-session files exist because two sessions on two branches each added to the same file (lines 9-15). A file written only by the runner where branches meet does not have that problem.

Cost of keeping the rule: «`tasks/RENUMBERED.md` appears only after a `journal.py fold`, which nothing calls by itself», so the file the task names for the owner does not exist until a manual fold, and the documents must explain `journal.py show renumbered`. Lines 33-35 confirm the runner calls no fold.
P7 forbids building «на виріст»; line 24 (N3) says tasks are handed out by one place, the task board through the runner.

Reason it might still hold: two runners on two clones would each write the map and conflict on `pull --rebase`, and reusing journal.py is cheap (one more `JOURNALS` entry, feature doc K10). The owner read design §6 in full, so this is the owner's call, not a removal.
